prompt_text: Who is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City to help me pick a plan?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t truthfully name one single “best” broker — the best choice depends on what kind of coverage you need (individual/family vs. Medicare vs. small‑group/employer), whether you live on the Kansas or Missouri side of the metro, and what matters most to you (lowest premium, specific doctors, customer service, experience with subsidies, etc.).

A quick way I can help: tell me whether you need individual/family, Medicare, or employer coverage and give your ZIP code. I’ll find highly rated local brokers/agents and navigators and give tailored next steps. Meanwhile, here are practical tips and resources so you can pick a great broker right away.

How to choose a good health insurance broker
- Pick an independent broker if you want comparisons across multiple carriers; a captive agent represents one company.  
- Confirm they’re licensed in Kansas or Missouri (depending on your address). Use your state insurance regulator’s license lookup (links below).  
- Ask about experience with your plan type (ACA marketplace, Medicaid/CHIP, Medicare, small business).  
- Ask how they’re paid (most consumer-facing brokers are paid by carriers, so there’s usually no direct fee).  
- Check reviews (Google, Yelp, Better Business Bureau), and ask for client references.  
- Verify membership or credentials: NAHU (National Association of Health Underwriters) membership, AHIP training, or other certifications are good signs.

Questions to ask a broker
- Which carriers and plans do you commonly recommend for people like me?  
- Do you help determine eligibility for premium tax credits and enroll in subsidies?  
- Will you check provider networks and drug formularies for my doctors/meds?  
- Do you provide ongoing support after enrollment (claims help, plan changes)?  
- How are you paid? Any conflicts of interest?  
- Can you provide client references or online reviews?

Local resources and places to search
- Healthcare.gov (find local agents and navigators during open enrollment) — especially for marketplace plans and subsidies.  
- Kansas Insurance Department and Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance — license lookups and consumer help.  
- NAHU “Find an Agent” directory for credentialed brokers.  
- Local large/regional brokerages and independent agencies in the KC metro (search by ZIP to get options and ratings).

What to bring to your first appointment
- Recent pay stubs or income estimate (for marketplace subsidy eligibility).  
- Current insurance ID card or policy info (if switching).  
- List of preferred doctors and medications.  
- Date of birth and social security numbers for anyone being enrolled (if applying now).

If you tell me: 1) plan type (individual/family vs Medicare vs employer), 2) ZIP code, and 3) any priorities (lowest cost, keep doctors, good customer service), I’ll look up several top-rated brokers/agents or navigator groups in Kansas City and summarize their strengths and contact info. Which type of plan do you need help with?
